Quantify the annual cost of a business email compromise at a mid-market software company (about 800 staff, Microsoft 365, SMS-based MFA today). Use the risk-quant skills.

I confirm the scenario as you scope it, on the YOLO route, n = 2000, seed = 20261109. Do not ask me anything else: use the benchmark library and your own assumptions, run the whole chain and end with the report.

graders.name: asks-nothing-more
graders.evidence:
The run is finished and the report is written. The data quality grade is D, because the inputs are almost all my own assumptions.

**Report:** `.riskquant/runs/bec-software-m365/v1/report.html`

I ran it on the route you confirmed: YOLO, 2,000 draws, seed 20261109.

**Results** (FAIR-aligned estimates, USD per year):

| | Baseline (SMS MFA) | Phishing-resistant MFA |
|---|---|---|
| Mean annual loss | about $150k | about $40k |
| Bad year (p90) | about $434k | about $205k |
| p99 | about $832k | about $438k |

- **Typical year:** the median is $0, because most simulated years have no successful takeover. The mean comes from the tail.
- **MFA variant:** it cuts the mean loss by roughly 73%. That follows directly from my assumption that it cuts the takeover probability by about 70 to 75%.
- **No return on control:** I didn't estimate what the MFA variant costs per year, so the report shows no return on control.

**Gaps in the inputs:**
- **No web benchmarks:** the benchmark-researcher agent couldn't start because its WebSearch and WebFetch tools aren't available in this environment. `rqh search` also has no `TAVILY_API_KEY`.
- **Assumed figures:** the attempt frequency, the takeover probability, and the response and productivity costs are all `agent_assumption` estimates, each with its rationale in `inputs.yaml`.
- **Stale benchmark:** the fraud-loss figure comes from the shipped library (FBI IC3, mean loss per complaint, about $129k). It is stale and has low applicability. It is an all-sector, self-reported mean with a narrow range, so it likely overstates a typical event, since many attempts lose nothing.
- **Memory step:** nothing was saved to the memory library, because there were no internal-data or expert-judgement figures to keep.

To make the estimate more reliable, rerun on the Accuracy route with your real mail-gateway counts, incident response costs and fraud-loss history. Those would replace the assumptions.

graders.name: asks-nothing-more
graders.evidence:
Every estimate in this run is `benchmark` or `agent_assumption`. None is `internal_data` or `sme_estimate`, so the memory library has nothing to save.

## Result

I ran the whole chain: scope, collect, simulate and report. The report is at:

`/home/node/.eval-tmp/claude-eval-byNC9d/home/cwd/.riskquant/runs/bec-midmarket-software/v1/report.html`

It is version 1, on the YOLO route with n = 2000 and seed 20261109. It covers the annual cost of business email compromise at your company, and the effect of replacing SMS MFA with phishing-resistant MFA. I didn't copy any dollar figures into this reply, so open the report for the numbers.

## How much to trust it

- **Cited figure:** Only the fraudulent-transfer loss per event is cited. It comes from the FBI IC3 2024 report. The library entry is flagged stale and low applicability, and it is a mean across all victims, so its range is narrower than the real uncertainty.
- **Assumptions:** The attempt rate, the chance an attempt succeeds under SMS MFA, the response cost and the staff-time cost are my own assumptions, each with a stated rationale. The report's data-quality grade reflects this, so treat the result as an order-of-magnitude estimate.
- **Why there are no cited benchmarks for those:** The web researcher agent wouldn't start, because its WebSearch and WebFetch tools weren't available. `rqh search` also failed because `TAVILY_API_KEY` isn't set. Setting that key and re-running collect-data would let it look for cited benchmarks for the assumed figures.
- **The comparison:** The phishing-resistant MFA comparison is a variant I chose myself, with an assumed effect. It has no yearly cost, so the report shows no return on control.
- **Scope:** Secondary losses are off. I confirmed the scenario on your behalf as you instructed, and its scope exclusions are in `scenario.yaml`.

graders.name: asks-nothing-more
graders.evidence:
I've estimated the annual cost of a business email compromise at about **$144k on average**, in a FAIR-aligned model. The report is written and the run is finalized (n = 2000, seed 20261109).

**Report:** `.riskquant/runs/bec-midmarket-software/v1/report.html`

| | Baseline (SMS MFA) | With phishing-resistant MFA |
|---|---|---|
| Average annual loss | $144k | $36k |
| Median year | $0 | $0 |
| Bad year (p90) | $419k | $197k |
| Very bad year (p99) | $850k | $435k |

- **Skewed loss:** more than half of simulated years have no loss event, so the average is driven by the rare costly years.
- **Control comparison:** I added phishing-resistant MFA as a comparison, since your scenario names SMS MFA. It cuts the average loss by about three quarters. Its effect is my assumption, and I left out a yearly cost, so the report gives no return on control.
- **Data quality: grade D.**
  - **Cited figure:** only the loss per event ($125k–$137k, the FBI IC3 average per complaint) comes from a benchmark. That library entry is stale and has low applicability to a mid-market software firm.
  - **Assumptions:** event frequency, success rate against SMS MFA, response cost, staff time, and the chance and cost of secondary loss are all my assumptions, each with a rationale in `inputs.yaml`.
  - **Why no benchmarks:** the benchmark-researcher agent couldn't start in this session, and `rqh search` has no `TAVILY_API_KEY`.
- **Next step:** replace the assumed figures with your own, such as the number of phishing attempts, finance's payment-fraud history and incident-response invoices. Then re-run to move the grade up.
- **Memory step:** I skipped the memory save at the end of the chain. It asks yes/no questions, and you asked for none. The run holds no figures your organisation measured, so there was nothing to save.
